patients.label: 45-year-old female with bladder leiomyosarcoma

identity_evidence.quote: Here, we present a case of bladder leiomyosarcoma in a well-preserved female

attribution_limitations: The source states that the initial diagnosis of metastatic disease in paraaortic nodes was revised and that the initial staging was revised, but gives no revised stage and does not say the nodes were benign; the nodal histology is described as granulomas secondary to tumor antigen.
Pelvic lymphadenectomy and paraaortic sampling were advised, but the source does not state that they were performed; later text mentions histology of pelvic and paraaortic nodes.

The Fig. 5 caption gives the largest lesion as 12.5 × 11.7 × 11.5 cm (SUVmax 13.8) in the left lumbar region, while the text gives the largest pelvic serosal deposit as 7.3 × 4.6 cm (SUVmax 13.8). The locations differ and the source does not say they are one lesion.
The text calls the finding a progressive intraabdominal (left lumbar) soft tissue swelling proven metastatic on cytology, while the Fig. 4 caption calls the aspirate source a peritoneal deposit.

The histopathology sentence says the picture suggested metastatic leiomyosarcoma at the anastomotic site, whereas the abstract and discussion state metastases in the anastomotic site and intestinal mucosa without hedging.

The discussion says the possibility of contamination during specimen retrieval cannot be ruled out and that aggressive biology was possibly the more probable cause of the rapid course; these are author speculation.
The Fig. 1 caption names aortocaval nodes on the baseline CT; the baseline text sentence lists only pelvic and paraaortic nodes (aortocaval nodes appear later in the intraoperative description).
The discussion says aggressive local adjuvant therapy was offered for close margins and perivesical extension; the narrative names adjuvant radiotherapy but does not itself give that indication.
